explanation: A eukaryotic chromosome is composed of a single double-helix DNA molecule. Proteins make up more than 50% of the chromosome's composition. While some of these proteins are enzymes involved in DNA and RNA synthesis, the vast majority are histones, which play a structural role in wrapping and packaging the chromosome. There are five primary types of histone proteins: H1, H2A, H2B, H3, and H4. The structures of H3 and H4 are highly conserved across different organisms, reflecting their essential, survival-critical functions that have been preserved throughout evolutionary history.
